faq.q: What is LLM model quantization?
faq.a: LLM quantization converts a model's weights, and often its activations, from 16-bit floating point into lower-bit formats like INT8 or INT4. This shrinks memory use and speeds up inference, at some cost in accuracy that depends heavily on the method and bitwidth chosen.

faq.q: What is the best quantization method for LLMs?
faq.a: There is no single best method: it depends on hardware and workload. Broad benchmarking found W8A8-FP is close to lossless on FP8-capable hardware, while GPTQ or AWQ at 4-bit weight-only remain the standard choice for memory-constrained local inference.

faq.q: When should you quantize a model?
faq.a: Quantize when memory, bandwidth, or latency limits are blocking deployment, such as running a large model on a single consumer GPU or reducing serving costs at scale. If you have headroom on all three, quantization adds risk without a clear payoff.

faq.q: How do I quantize a model?
faq.a: Export the model at full precision, choose a PTQ method suited to your bitwidth and hardware, build a calibration set that mirrors your real traffic, then run a maintained tool like AutoGPTQ or llmcompressor. Validate with perplexity and task-specific benchmarks before rolling the quantized model into production.
